decision: Activate BINDER-MODEL-PILOT-1 for staged source/reuse and exact API/fragment preparation. The current candidate seams are official Lean 4.33.0 Expr lifting/instantiation and Kiota 2d2a9fa expression shift/instantiation; source identities and the common fragment must be frozen before model construction. No scientific vectors or observers are authorized before those gates and the independent model/translation audit.

categories.assessment: The selected independent finite model provides expectations beyond within-checker agreement and may reuse prior small-term infrastructure. Build-mode conformance remains a plausible but less immediately specified alternative; resource-envelope work has higher setup cost and no current discrepancy trigger.

The completed valid-term generator and capture-avoiding primitives can seed reusable operation vectors, while Lean4Lean offers formalization lemmas but cannot act as the independent oracle. Preserve model/API limitations and every unsupported disposition.

No new substantive upstream feedback was evidenced in the dated ledger during this local entry review. Kiota/Nanoda follow-up remains held under owner direction; this item requires no external contact.

The exact Lean Expr APIs and candidate Kiota expression operations need focused source binding and a supported common fragment. Existing Lean4Lean source and valid-dependent-term assets are concrete reuse leads, not semantic authority; a current literature/reuse assessment remains an active preparation gate.

Source binding, supported operation signatures, fragment agreement, named-variable capture avoidance, translation audit and independent negative-capable expectations are tractable work inside this active item. Build-mode and resource alternatives retain their own unpassed scientific entry gates.

candidates.rationale: Selected because a separate named-variable model can yield independent expectations for a fixed shared fragment. Preparation can decide and bind exact supported APIs and translation rules before any scientific vector or observer launch.
